examples.title: LED blinker with a 555
examples.description: An astable NE555 flashing an LED, with a ground plane on the back. Through-hole parts, 46 x 30 mm.

examples.title: Arduino Uno shield
examples.description: A shield for the Uno (68.6 x 53.3 mm, four mounting holes): an LED on D13 with its resistor and a button on D2.

examples.title: ESP32 breakout
examples.description: An ESP32-WROOM-32 module with decoupling, an enable pull-up and sixteen GPIOs on two headers.

examples.title: 5 V power supply (LM7805)
examples.description: A linear 5 V supply: LM7805 in a TO-220, a reverse-polarity diode, an input and an output electrolytic, a power LED with its resistor and screw terminals, 58 x 34 mm with a ground plane.

examples.title: ATtiny85 breakout
examples.description: An ATtiny85 in a DIP-8 socket with a decoupling capacitor, a reset pull-up, an LED on PB1 and every pin on a header, 42 x 30 mm.

examples.title: LED bar graph (10 LEDs)
examples.description: Ten LEDs in a row, each with its 220 ohm resistor, driven from one 1x10 header (Arduino pins D2 to D11) on a two-layer board with a ground plane, 72 x 34 mm.

examples.title: USB-to-UART header breakout
examples.description: Moves the six-pin FTDI cable header (GND CTS VCC TXD RXD DTR) to a four-pin UART header with TX and RX crossed over and a 100 nF bypass capacitor. The reference names on the silkscreen label the headers.

examples.title: LM358 non-inverting amplifier
examples.description: One half of an LM358 (DIP-8) as a gain-of-11 amplifier: 10 k and 1 k set the gain, the second op-amp is parked as a follower, with input, output and supply headers and ground planes on both sides, 44 x 32 mm.
